races.title: State Assembly, District 42
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Deborah Klein Lopez
cands.bio: Agoura Hills City Council member, elected in 2018. She has served as Mayor and is Mayor Pro Tem. Chair of Clean Power Alliance. Agoura High School graduate with a bachelor's degree from Northwestern University. Democratic candidate for California State Assembly District 42.

endorsements.text: Endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the California Democratic Party, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the California Nurses Association, the California Teachers Association, the National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, Reproductive Freedom For All, and the Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.

In her own survey she lists LA County Firefighters Local 1014, Planned Parenthood Central Coast Action Fund, National Latino Peace Officers Association Ventura County, US Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff, Rep. Julia Brownley and Assemblywoman Jacqui Irwin (the current AD 42 incumbent).

cands.gaps: Her birthplace and the year she came to California are not stated in the sources we had. We found no documented actions in office, such as sponsored measures or council votes, only her own survey statements. We found nothing on her position on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, gun laws, abortion restrictions, school choice or police pay. Her statements on growth and development are general. She says she will work with cities and counties to find resources to accommodate growth, but she takes no clear position on slowing or limiting it. We found no controversies or foreign ties. Her claims about leading a school-funding ballot measure and chairing Clean Power Alliance come from her own survey and were not independently confirmed.

cands.name: Ted Nordblum
cands.bio: Republican small business owner from Newbury Park. He has owned Titan Medical, a Thousand Oaks medical device company, for about 20 years. Earlier he was a union heavy equipment operator and also worked as an actor and voice actor. He ran for Assembly District 42 in 2022, 2024 and 2026 and has held no public office.

endorsements.text: Sheriff Jim Fryhoff is quoted on the campaign site: "Ted Nordblum is the common-sense leader we need to fight for our values in Sacramento."
The Republican Party of California endorsed him in the 2024 race, per Ballotpedia.

In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he listed (self-reported, partial list) endorsements from the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association PAC, the California Rifle and Pistol Association, the Ventura County Republican Party and Sen. Shannon Grove.

cands.gaps: We could not confirm where Nordblum was raised or when he moved to California. His campaign site says he came to California and has lived in the Conejo Valley for over two decades. A 2022 survey answer says over 50 years. He has held no public office, so there is no legislative record to review. We found no documented stance from him on data centers, development or growth, and no controversies in the pages we read. His public statements on most policy areas are limited to general campaign-site language.
